CHROMIUM: tpm: move shutdown logic from common code The shutdown logic is moved from the common gentle shutdown notifier to device-specific .shutdown handlers. This is done because the current shutdown notifier prevents sending any commands to tpm after it is called, and we need to send vendor-specific commands during shutdown. The new shutdown handlers still prevent sending further commands to the tpm after they are called. But the method is different: Instead of locking and never releasing chip->tpm_mutex, we now rely on the standard tpm_chip_unregister(), which among other things (1) internally acquires chip->ops_sem and clears out chip->ops, (2) unregisters sysfs entries. The common tpm driver code already makes sure that all calls from its external interface (through /dev/tpm0 or through exported symbols like tpm_get_random()) go through chip->ops while holding chip_ops_sem. Except for sysfs, but those sysfs entries are also unregistered in tpm_chip_unregister(). So, calling tpm_chip_unregister() makes sure there are no incomplete tpm transfers, and commands can't be sent to the tpm in the future. Thus, a tpm, for which tpm_chip_unregister() is called in its shutdown handler, can't be then reset in the middle of processing a command and go into the defensive lockout state as a result. To satisfy the tests: "[gentle shutdown]" printout is removed from the common code that no longer guarantees it. And added to individual drivers, which call tpm_chip_unregister() from their shutdown handlers. BUG=chrome-os-partner:59007 TEST=shutdown on devices with tpm 1.2 and tpm 2.0 running 4.4 kernel, verify that the shutdown handler is called. CHROMIUM: tpm: control deep-sleep for cr50 Deep-sleep enabling/disabling logic for cr50 devices: - At boot / when initializing (in driver's probe): disable. - When suspending: -- enable, if suspend is controlled by firmware (firmware will re-initialize the TPM on resume); -- disable otherwise. - When resuming: disable. - During shutdown / when removing device: enable. Put deep-sleep-related code into cr50.c/cr50.h shared by cr50_i2c and cr50_spi. BUG=chrome-os-partner:59007 TEST=1) Firmware-controlled suspend (S3 for x86, none otherwise): echo 0 > /sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm echo "+10" > /sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm echo mem > /sys/power/state In cr50 console, verify "enable deep-sleep" is sent on suspend, "disable deep-sleep" on resume. 2) Suspend without firmware involvement (S0ix for x86, all otherwise): echo 0 > /sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm echo "+10" > /sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm echo freeze > /sys/power/state In cr50 console, verify "disable deep-sleep" is sent on suspend and resume. 3) Shutdown. In cr50 console, verify "enable deep-sleep" is sent during shutdown. Change-Id: Iae039b76611149523cf9cd6b426169bf88ad4b6b Signed-off-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/427372 Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com>

release_stages: Fixup PaygenTest stage naming. Recently, the Paygen stage was split up into substages: PaygenBuild and PaygenTest. In order to make things clearer on the waterfall, the channel of the payloads being generated was added to the stage name, however, for the PaygenTest stage, it had an extra suffix of '-channel'. This commit fixes that. The stage names should now be PaygenBuildFoo and PaygenTestFoo. Additionally, this commit also fixes the unit tests to prevent polluting the source directory with 'foo-build_uri' files as well as 'archive_build_uri' directory. firmware_ECBootTime: Prevent dropped power on cmd. firmware_ECBootTime was just checking to see if the EC was up and then immediately sending the EC command to power on the system. However, it's very possible that the console task isn't quite ready at that point in time and the power on command may be dropped. This will result in a faulty test failure. This commit changes the test such that it waits for the string printed by the console task indicating that it's ready. This string is the following: "Console is enabled" This should be much more robust than just searching for "Inits done". BUG=chrome-os-partner:59923= BRANCH=None TEST=Run firmware_ECBootTime against chell and verify it passes. TEST=Change the queried string to one that is not printed and verify that the test fails. Change-Id: I0aa0132ff95272b909ef2951cc31a29b2fa04f8e Signed-off-by: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/428184 Commit-Ready: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@chromium.org> Tested-by: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com>
